transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Overnight a federal judge ordered the White House to restore access to three media organizations.
President Trump banned CNN, MS Now and Politico last week.
All three of those outlets now say some of their journalists have not been permitted
to get into the White House this morning.
It is not yet clear why.
President Trump welcomes China's President Xi Jinping to the White House today.
Iran, trade and the future of AI are expected to be among the issues discussed.
And Piers Emily Feng reports this is Xi's first state visit to the U.S. in more than
a decade.
Trump and Xi will hold bilateral meetings on tariffs and the war on Iran.
The two countries are trying to maintain what China calls "strategic stability," a
detente in the relationship.
And just before the meetings this week, the U.S. announced a two-month extension of a
trade truce that lets it access Chinese-made rare earth products.
But other sources of tension remain, including new Chinese actions designed to block U.S.
sanctions and recent U.S. legal actions against importing and selling Chinese drones and Internet
routers.
Emily Feng and Pure News, Washington.
Bo Xi and Trump are likely to discuss the war against Iran and Russia's war against
Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the U.N. General Assembly Russia's war is
spreading and threatens the world.
And Piers Michelle Kellerman reports the Ukrainian leader supports Trump's call for both Russia
and Ukraine to stop hitting each other's energy facilities.
In the Russia-Ukraine war, at least, Zelensky's been proposing this kind of energy ceasefire
because Trump has been unhappy with Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure.
But the Ukrainians obviously want the Russians to stop attacking Ukraine's energy grids ahead
of another tough winter.
And they also want to allow grain to be exported as before.
And Piers Michelle Kellerman reporting.
Israeli authorities say a Palestinian attack has seriously wounded the son of Israel's
ambassador to the United States.
And Piers Daniel Estrin reports.
The Israeli army says a Palestinian driver rammed a car into a group of security forces
checking vehicles at a checkpoint in the West Bank.
Israeli forces shot and killed the driver.
The soldier wounded in the attack is the son of Israeli ambassador to the U.S. Yechiel
Leiter.
He said on X that his son is being treated in a hospital and, quote, "needs a miracle."
The ambassador's other son was killed in 2023 as a soldier fighting in the Gaza war.
It's an especially tense moment in the West Bank.
Earlier this week, a Palestinian gunman killed an Israeli settler.
There's been a wave of Israeli settler violence against Palestinians.
Israel has deployed large numbers of troops in the West Bank, fearing an explosion of
violence ahead of national elections next month.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Detectives in Idaho solved a decades-long cold case, which they say may also have connections
to the 1982 Tylenol murders, Jackson Holmes of Boise State Public Radio reports.
In 1982, a man killed himself with cyanide in a Boise church.
He carried no identification.
Then, in 2019, Detective Tim Cooper connected the case to a Jacksonville, Florida man who
went missing that same year.
Through family DNA matching, officials determined he was Matthew Francis Betkowski, an organic
chemist.
Cooper says Betkowski's history with cyanide drew him to September of 1982, when seven
people in Chicago died after taking cyanide-laced Tylenol.
Forensic psychiatrist Park Diaz asked other forensic scientists nationwide if they believed
this Boise case could be connected.
Overwhelmingly, they regarded him as a viable suspect.
A few were convinced that he was the killer.
The Ada County Sheriff's Office says they've given all information to the Illinois agencies
involved in the Tylenol poisonings.
For NPR News, I'm Jackson Holmes.
Disgraced film executive Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison in
his re-trial on sex crimes in New York.
He was first convicted in 2020, but that was thrown out on appeal.
New York prosecutors have re-tried him ever since.
Separately, Weinstein was convicted of rape in California.
He was sentenced there to 16 years in prison.
However, a California court has ruled that he will be re-sentenced.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.

topics.text: Federal judge orders White House to restore media access for CNN, MS Now, and Politico
President Trump welcomes China's President Xi Jinping to White House for first state visit in over a decade
U.S. and China extend two-month trade truce allowing access to Chinese rare earth products
Ukrainian President Zelensky supports Trump's call for Russia and Ukraine to stop attacking energy facilities
Palestinian driver rams car into Israeli security forces at West Bank checkpoint, injures ambassador's son
Idaho detectives solve decades-old cold case, identify victim as organic chemist with possible Tylenol connections
Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison following New York sex crimes retrial
